newsitem.title: USA: Brazil's Lampreia sees 1996 FDI at $9.0 billion.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Lampreia sees 1996 FDI at $9.0 billion.

text.p: Brazil's Minister of External Relations Luiz Felipe Lampreia said on Wednesday he expects foreign direct investment in Brazil to total $9.0 billion in 1996.

"So far we have got something around $6.0 billion and we are projecting $9.0 billion (in foreign direct investment) for the entire year," Lampreia told an audience of businessmen and diplomats gathered here.
"About 40 percent of that comes from the U.S.," Lampreia added.
The minister said foreign direct investment in Brazil totaled $3.0 billion in 1995 and $1.0 billion in 1994.
Lampreia said Brazil's economy is currently growing at an annual rate of between 4.0 and 5.0 percent, which he said is consistent with 1.7/1.8 percent population growth.
"It's still not enough, but it's a great step into consolidating the middle class," Lampreia said.
Lampreia said current fiscal and social security reforms being sought by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso are moving at a slow pace in congress.
He acknowledged the plan was "ambitious" and might not be achieved over the next one or two years.
"Clearly the kind of very ambitious program that the president has is not going to be achieved in one or two years," Lampreia said.

Using the reforms as an argument, Lampreia stressed the need for new legislation that would allow the reelection of President Cardoso. "Brazil needs continuity of programs ... This is why the president has now come to the conclusion to seek reelection."
Under current legislation, Brazilian presidents are not allowed to run for reelection.
